original_title: All readability formulas were normed on written text reading — none validated for listening
original_claim_MUST_NOT_BE_IMPORTED: Every standard readability formula (Flesch, SMOG, Gunning Fog, Flesch-Kincaid, ARI, Coleman-Liau, Dale-Chall) was developed for and validated against written prose comprehension. Grade levels do not transfer to spoken delivery. Specific problems: (1) Spoken scripts use fragments and delivery-cued sentences that break formula assumptions, (2) Syllable-based metrics assume reading difficulty, not listening difficulty, (3) Character-count metrics (ARI, Coleman-Liau) are meaningless for audio — the audience never sees the text, (4) Dale-Chall's "easy word" list reflects print vocabulary, not spoken vocabulary.

original_title: No existing text metrics measure the dimensions most critical for script quality
